question: The cost price of an article is increased by 15% and later the new price is decreased by 15%. If the latest price of the article is ₹19,550, find the original cost price of the article.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a value is increased by x% and then decreased by x%, there is always a net decrease of (x² ÷ 100)%.

Net percentage change = −(15 × 15) ÷ 100 = −2.25%.

Final price is (100 − 2.25)% = 97.75% of original CP.

97.75% of CP = ₹19,550

CP = (19550 × 100) ÷ 97.75 = ₹20,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase = 15%

Percentage decrease = 15%

Latest price = ₹19,550

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + Rate₁/100) × (1 − Rate₂/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the original cost price be ₹x.

⇒ Final Price = x × (1 + 15/100) × (1 − 15/100)

⇒ 19550 = x × (115/100) × (85/100)

⇒ 19550 = x × (23/20) × (17/20)

⇒ 19550 = x × (391/400)

⇒ x = (19550 × 400) ÷ 391

⇒ x = 50 × 400

⇒ x = 20000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes successive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is calculated using the formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Equal Successive Increase and Decrease

If a number is first increased by x% and then decreased by x%, there is always an overall decrease. The net decrease percentage is x² ÷ 100.

Multiplier / Ratio Method

This method is highly efficient for complex fractional percentages. Convert each percentage change into a fraction and multiply the initial value by all the respective multiplying factors to instantly arrive at the final value.
